newsitem.title: UK: Dec oil deliveries to key consumers off 0.6pct - IEA.
newsitem.headline: Dec oil deliveries to key consumers off 0.6pct - IEA.

text.p: Oil deliveries in the seven biggest consuming nations of the OECD fell 0.6 percent in December year-on-year to 34.05 million barrels per day (bpd), the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
The largest change was in residual fuel oil which fell some 12.5 percent from year earlier levels as gas grabbed a bigger share of the power generating market.
In the United States deliveries fell slightly overall in December but there was strong demand growth for jet/kerosene and other products and a moderate rise in gasoline deliveries.
These were not enough to offset big falls in residual fuel and heating oil deliveries.
Japan oil demand fell by more than 215,000 bpd or 3.4 percent due to falls in demand for all major products except LPG, naphtha and gasoline.
Deliveries of crude and residual fuel to power stations decreased by 18.6 percent and 16.5 percent respectively.
Oil deliveries in Italy during December fell for the fifth successive month due to weak economic growth and lower fuel deliveries to state power company Enel.
There was a 75,000 bpd drop in deliveries of residual fuel in Italy, caused primarily by lower deliveries to Enel, the IEA said in its Monthly Oil Market Report.
Electricity demand in 1996 was essentially unchanged with a rise of 11.5 percent in hydro output, no change in electricity imports and a fall of two percent in hydrocarbon generated power.
Increased supplies of gas from north Africa are believed to have led to increased gas use by the power generation sector largely at the expense of residual fuel oil, the IEA said.

In Germany demand rose for the sixth successive month with strong growth in diesel and heating oil deliveries more than offsetting falls of most other fuels. Total gas oil deliveries rose by 110,000 bpd or nearly nine percent, divided 70/30 between heating oil and diesel.
The 10 percent rise in heating oil deliveries is similar to the 12 month moving average and occurred despite retail prices being considerably higher than in the previous December.
Consumer stock data indicate that heating oil stocks fell during the month and closed some 13 million barrels lower than a year earlier.
UK oil demand rose by the greatest proportion since November 1993 with demand increasing for all products except "other products".

Deliveries of LPG and jet/kerosene rose by 10.6 percent and 8.4 percent respectively while naphtha jumped a huge 44.4 percent as larger users such as chemical companies switched away from high priced LPG as a feedstock.
Heavy fuel deliveries rose reflecting high gas prices. This contrast with a year earlier when lower gas prices meant a 25 percent fall in heavy fuel deliveries.
In France demand fell for the second successive month despite colder weather and higher industrial production.
The demand weakness was partly due to strong growth the previous December and poor driving conditions in the last week of the month.
Canadian demand fell 1.7 percent in December year-on-year, featuring a 12.6 percent rise in jet/kerosene and three percent fall in gasoline.
